editionNote: Evening edition. It covers the 24 hours to 17:10 CET on 28 October; new research covers 05:10 CET to 17:10 CET on 28 October, items from the previous edition still inside the 24 hours were carried, and stories with new developments are marked as follow-ups.

theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: Wednesday Drone Attack Kills a 60-Year-Old Man in Ukraine's Kharkiv
items.lede: The daylight strike, which hit the same district as the late-evening attack, left three men in hospital, according to the regional governor.

sections.text: A Russian attack drone struck Kharkiv's Osnovianskyi district again on Wednesday 28 October, starting a fire, Mayor Ihor Terekhov said [1][2]. Regional governor Oleh Syniehubov said a 60-year-old man was killed and three men aged 46, 56, and 41 were taken to hospital with injuries of varying severity [3][1][2]. Ukrainska Pravda said a 48-year-old woman also needed medical help [1]. No Russian comment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the death and the hospital count, because three Ukrainian outlets carry the same on-record figures from the mayor and the governor. The woman's treatment rests on one outlet.

items.title: Ukraine's General Staff Claims Strikes on a Tor System and Radar in Russia
items.lede: Kyiv says the hits in Kursk and Bryansk regions, plus a depot in occupied Donetsk, open gaps that its drones can exploit.

sections.text: Ukraine's General Staff said its forces struck three Russian air-defence assets on Russian territory on 27 October and overnight into 28 October, and a military supply depot near Valerianivka in occupied Donetsk region [4]. It named a Tor-M2 surface-to-air missile system near Rzhava and a radar station near Maloe Gorodkovoe in Russia's Kursk region, and an electronic-warfare station near Semyachky in Bryansk region [4]. It said each hit opens a temporary gap in Russian air defences for Ukrainian drones [4]. No Russian confirmation or damage assessment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is low on the results, because the claims rest on the Ukrainian military as relayed by Ukraine's state news agency, with no independent or Russian confirmation.

items.title: Ukraine's Air Defences Down 71 of 88 Russian Drones Overnight
items.lede: Russia also fired a ballistic missile from Taganrog, and weapons got through at eight sites while several drones were still airborne at 08:00 Kyiv time.

sections.text: Ukraine's Air Force said Russia attacked from 18:00 Kyiv time on 27 October (17:00 CET) with one Iskander-M or S-400 ballistic missile launched from Taganrog and 88 drones, 38 of them jet-powered, plus Gerbera and Parodiya-type decoy drones and S8000 Banderol/Dan-T missiles [5][6]. It said the drones came from the directions of Oryol and Kursk in Russia and Hvardiiske in occupied Crimea [5][7]. As of 08:00 Kyiv time on 28 October (07:00 CET), air defences had shot down or jammed 71 drones, including 31 jet-powered ones, while impacts were recorded at eight locations and debris fell at two more [5][7][6]. The Air Force did not say whether the missile was intercepted, and no Russian Defence Ministry account of the strike was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that the Air Force reported these figures, because three Ukrainian outlets carry the same statement. The totals rest on the Ukrainian military alone.

items.title: Kremlin Still Has No Date for Russia-Ukraine-US Talks in Abu Dhabi
items.lede: Moscow says it will announce the meeting once fixed, with a Putin aide pointing to mid-November and a source dismissing reports of 4 November.

sections.text: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on 27 October that no date had been set for new trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine, and the United States in Abu Dhabi [8][9]. A Kremlin readout of Putin's call that day with Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said all three welcomed an agreement to resume the talks in early to mid November, and that Putin insisted Russia's interests be met in full and without conditions [10]. On Wednesday afternoon Peskov said the Kremlin would announce the date once it is fixed [11][12]. Vesti said presidential aide Yury Ushakov had told it the talks are expected around the middle of November, with no exact date yet [12]. An unnamed source told TASS that coordination is under way and that reports of 4 November misread officials' remarks [13]. No Ukrainian or U.S. date was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that no date had been set by Wednesday afternoon, because Peskov said so on record on both days. The mid-November timing and Putin's terms rest on Russian official sources alone, and the TASS denial of 4 November rests on one unnamed source.

items.title: Ukraine and Russia Keep the Kherson-Region Truce Around Oleshky Into a Second Day
items.lede: Kyiv's human rights commissioner said on Wednesday both sides were still observing it, with a joint humanitarian mission planned before it expires on 1 November.

sections.text: Ukraine's General Staff said Ukraine began observing a ceasefire around Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in the Kherson region, from 03:00 Kyiv time on 27 October (02:00 CET), and the Kremlin said Russia halted fighting there an hour later Moscow time [14][9]. On Tuesday evening U.S. First Lady Melania Trump, who brokered the pause, said its area had been widened beyond Oleshky within the Kherson region to give aid convoys safe passage [15][16]. The BBC said a Kherson city official confirmed Russian shelling had stopped, that evacuations are planned for Friday, and that an estimated 1,700 to 2,000 people remain in Oleshky [17]. Lawmaker David Arakhamia said the pause runs until 22:59 Kyiv time on 1 November [18]. Ukraine's human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets, who reported full compliance on Tuesday evening, said on Wednesday both sides were still honouring the deal as of 12:00 Kyiv time, and that the pause allows a humanitarian mission with Russia's rights commissioner Yana Lantratova [19][20]. No figure for aid delivered was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that the pause is holding and was widened, because Ukrainian, Russian, and U.S. figures say so on record and the BBC reports local confirmation. The Friday evacuations rest on the BBC, and Wednesday's status on Lubinets alone.

items.title: Zelensky Says Russia Has Fired Over 100 Ballistic Missiles at Kyiv Since 14 October
items.lede: Ukraine's president added on Wednesday that Kyiv gets only about 12 Patriot interceptors a month and used 35 in October alone.
items.flag: FOLLOW UP TO PREVIOUS REPORT · single-source, unconfirmed

sections.text: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said in his evening video address on 27 October that Russia has launched more than 100 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and the Kyiv region since 14 October [21]. He said Ukraine currently lacks missiles for its Patriot systems and that partners' delivery delays make it hard to defend against ballistic strikes [21]. He said stronger air-defence support would leave Ukraine in a much better position, including diplomatically, and that Russian attacks continue on Dnipro, Zaporizhzhia, Odesa, Kharkiv, Sumy, and Kherson [21]. Speaking to journalists on Wednesday, he said Ukraine will receive on average 12 Patriot missiles a month in 2026 [22]. He said a U.S. package of 12 missiles had been signed by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, but that Ukraine had used 35 this month and had to find the other 23 elsewhere [22]. No independent count of the missiles was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because both statements rest on Zelensky's own words as reported by Ukraine's state news agency, with no independent count of the missiles or of Patriot deliveries.

items.title: Russian Drone Hits an Apartment Block in Ukraine's Kharkiv, Injuring a Boy of Four
items.lede: Rescuers later counted five injured and said the blaze spread across 2,500 square metres, damaging garages, cars, and nearby high-rise homes.

sections.text: A Russian drone struck Kharkiv's Osnovianskyi district in Ukraine at about 22:40 Kyiv time on 27 October (21:40 CET), hitting an apartment building where Mayor Ihor Terekhov said people were trapped [23][24]. Regional governor Oleh Syniehubov said a woman aged 32, a woman aged 65, a man aged 56, and a four-year-old boy were injured, and three were taken to hospital [25][23]. He said the strike set fire to a two-storey industrial building, a two-storey apartment building, and a one-storey house, and damaged another home and a car [25][26]. On Wednesday morning Ukraine's State Emergency Service said the number injured had risen to five, including the four-year-old, and that the jet-powered drone's impact started a fire covering 2,500 square metres [27][28]. It said multi-storey homes, garages, and cars were also damaged [27]. No Russian comment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the strike and the injury count, because several outlets carry the same on-record figures from the mayor, the regional governor, and the emergency service.

items.title: Russian Submarine Test-Fires a Bulava Intercontinental Missile From the Sea of Okhotsk
items.lede: The Defence Ministry says the warheads hit their target range in the Arkhangelsk region on time during what it called routine combat training.

sections.text: Russia's Defence Ministry said early on 28 October that the Pacific Fleet nuclear submarine Generalissimus Suvorov, a Borei-A class boat, fired a Bulava intercontinental ballistic missile from a submerged position in the Sea of Okhotsk [29][30]. It said the warheads reached the Chizha range in Russia's Arkhangelsk region on time, and called the launch part of planned combat training [29][30]. No launch time was given, and no Western or Ukrainian comment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that the ministry announced the launch, but its account of the result rests on Russian state media alone, with no independent confirmation.

items.title: Russia's Defence Ministry Claims 293 Ukrainian Drones Downed in a Day
items.lede: Moscow's airports worked under flight limits, and Bryansk's governor reported more than 200 flats damaged, while Kyiv made no matching claim by the cutoff.

sections.text: Russia's Defence Ministry said on the evening of 27 October that air defences downed 71 Ukrainian drones, and 293 over the full day [31]. Russia's aviation agency said Vnukovo, Domodedovo, and Zhukovsky airports near Moscow were handling flights only with clearance because of temporary airspace restrictions [32]. Regional governors reported men injured by drones in Kursk region's Lgov and in Bryansk region, and Bryansk's governor said more than 200 flats in the city were damaged in the 27 October attack, according to Sever-Press [33]. Sever-Press also reported that two men were killed by explosive devices in Bryansk's Bezhitsky district [33]. No Ukrainian claim of targets hit was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is low on the drone totals, because they rest on the Russian Defence Ministry alone. Confidence is moderate on the airport limits and local damage, which come from Russian officials relayed by Russian outlets.

theaters.heading: Sabotage, drones, cyber, disinformation, and espionage targeting European states

items.title: Poland Indicts a Citizen Accused of Spying for Russian Civilian Intelligence
items.lede: Poland's ABW security agency says the man, placed among Polish and European lawmakers from 2016 to 2021, spread propaganda and spotted recruits for Moscow.

sections.text: Poland's Internal Security Agency (ABW) said on Wednesday that its investigation of Janusz N., a Polish citizen suspected of spying for Russian intelligence, has ended with an indictment [1]. The agency said that from 2016 to 2021, while placed among Polish and European lawmakers, he carried out paid tasks for Russia's civilian intelligence service, including propaganda, disinformation, and political provocations [1]. It said he acted in Poland, including in Olsztyn, in other EU states, and in Azerbaijan, Ukraine, and Moldova, aimed at Poland's support for Ukraine's pro-Western course, and identified people for recruitment by a Russian intelligence collaborator [1]. The case involved a Joint Investigation Team and was supervised by the National Prosecutor's Office [1]. No court date was given.
Confidence is high that the ABW announced the indictment, which is on its own site. The espionage allegations are the prosecution's and are untested in court; no second outlet was read.

items.title: Three Sea Drones Strike a Container Ship in Bulgaria's Black Sea Waters
items.lede: All 18 crew of the Liberian-flagged Contship Jet were rescued and taken to Varna, and Bulgarian officials named no attacker in the reports read.

sections.text: Bulgaria's Defence Minister Dimitar Stoyanov said on Wednesday that three maritime drones struck the Liberian-flagged container ship Contship Jet in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone, about 21 miles from Shabla, speaking after talks in Sofia with his Turkish and Romanian counterparts on Black Sea security [2][3]. The rescue centre in Constanța received the report at 12:01 Sofia time (11:01 CET), and the crew abandoned ship at 12:13 [2]. The ship was sailing from Haifa, Israel, to Constanța, Romania, with 421 containers on board, according to the crew [2]. Bulgaria's Transport Ministry said all 18 crew were rescued by Navy and Border Police vessels and taken to Varna [3]. Neither report named who launched the drones.
Confidence is high on the strike and the rescue, which Bulgaria's defence and transport ministers stated on record and two Bulgarian outlets carried. No attribution was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Moldova's Prime Minister Calls a Cyberattack on State Services Coordinated and Large-Scale
items.lede: About 750,000 records yielded at least one personal data element, Vasile Tofan said, adding that investigators are examining possible foreign state involvement.

sections.text: Moldova's Prime Minister Vasile Tofan told Wednesday's government meeting that attacks on public digital services between 19 and 23 October targeted about one million personal identification numbers (IDNPs) [4]. He said preliminary data show that at least one data element, such as a name or year of birth, was extracted in about 750,000 cases, which he said did not mean 750,000 accounts were hacked [4]. Tofan said the attackers exploited vulnerabilities and automated the extraction, that artificial intelligence allegedly helped them find the flaws, and that bank card data were not compromised [4]. He said the services were investigating the possible involvement of foreign state actors and warned of follow-on social engineering by SMS, email, and phone [4]. No state was named by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the figures come from the prime minister's on-record statement as carried by the state news agency, and no second outlet or technical report was read.

items.title: Poland and Germany Hold Three Suspects in Romania's Russia-Linked Brașov Arson Case
items.lede: A Ukrainian was detained in Warsaw on a Romanian warrant, and the two Belarusians held in Bavaria reportedly also plotted fires near a Nuremberg rail line.

sections.text: Romania's Intelligence Service (SRI) said on 26 October that a sabotage network coordinated from Russia set the 14 September fire on the Carfil industrial platform in Brașov, next to a subsidiary of state arms maker Romarm [5][6]. On Tuesday Romania summoned Russia's ambassador, Vladimir Lipaev, over what its Foreign Ministry called a clear act of hybrid warfare [7], and the Russian Embassy said Lipaev rejected the unsubstantiated accusations [8]. A spokesman for Poland's Central Investigation Bureau (CBŚP) told Polsat News on Wednesday that officers detained the Ukrainian suspect late on Monday afternoon under a Romanian European Arrest Warrant [9]. Notes from Poland, citing RMF FM sources, reported that the 25-year-old, named as Artem S., picked the target and arranged payment, and that a Polish court will rule on extradition [10]. Der Spiegel reported on Wednesday afternoon that the two Belarusians, aged 39 and 50, have been in custody in Bavaria since early October on suspicion of planning to set fires near a railway line and a power line around Nuremberg [11][12].

Confidence is high on the Warsaw detention, which Poland's CBŚP confirmed on record. The Nuremberg plot rests on Der Spiegel's security sources as relayed by dts, and the Russian direction rests on Romanian intelligence; neither is independently confirmed.

items.title: Hackers Hit Italy's Chamber of Deputies Mail System, Including Meloni's Deputy Inbox
items.lede: La Repubblica says hackers read the emails of Meloni and two other right-wing lawmakers, while Rome prosecutors wait on a police report before opening a case.

sections.text: Italy's Chamber of Deputies said its computer systems came under a large-scale cyberattack in recent days that involved the mailboxes of numerous lawmakers, including Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's account as a deputy, ANSA reported on Tuesday [13]. Palazzo Chigi sources said that mailbox is not the one Meloni uses for government communications [13] [14]. Chamber sources called the matter not an emergency and a daily occurrence, said protective measures were in place with the National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) under a specific protocol, and said some system functions could be switched off temporarily [13]. The same sources said similar attempts had intensified in recent days against other national, European, and international institutions [13] [14]. Rome prosecutors are awaiting a first report from the Postal Police and will open a case for unauthorized access to a computer system [15]. La Repubblica reported on Tuesday evening that the emails of Meloni, of Delmastro, and of League lawmaker Formentini were read, and that the method, the depth of access, and the choice of targets point to a targeted operation [16]. No attribution to any actor had been made public by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the attack and Meloni's mailbox, which ANSA and Chamber sources confirm. That the emails were read rests on la Repubblica's summary alone.

theaters.heading: Politics, security, and defense across the EU and NATO's European members

items.title: Britain's Chancellor Healey Targets Energy Bills in Burnham Government's First Budget
items.lede: Twenty million English households get a one-off payment and banks face a doubled profit surcharge, in a package NOS called restrained.

sections.text: UK Chancellor John Healey presented on Wednesday the first Budget since Andy Burnham became prime minister, the BBC reported [1]. It gives a one-off 100-pound payment to 20 million lower-band households in England for energy bills, removes standing charges from household gas bills, extends the fuel-duty freeze and the VAT cut on electricity bills to July, and raises the minimum wage and the new state pension by 3.9 per cent from April [1]. The surcharge on bank profits rises from 3 to 6 per cent for 15 months from January, and gambling-machine taxes rise [1]. NOS called it a left-leaning but restrained package of modest spending and modest tax rises focused on the cost of living [2].
Confidence is high on the measures, listed by the BBC from the Budget and matched by NOS; the characterisation of the package is NOS's own.

items.title: At Least 68 Killed as Spanish AVE Train Rear-Ends Stopped Iryo Train Near Toledo
items.lede: Transport Minister Óscar Puente blamed a control-centre order to resume full speed after a signalling failure, calling it inexplicable.

sections.text: Spain's state-run Renfe AVE high-speed train ran into the back of a stationary private Iryo train on the Madrid–Andalusia line in Toledo province at about 08:53 on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people, El País reported [3][4]. The AVE carried 397 passengers and the Iryo 147 [3]. Transport Minister Óscar Puente said the LZB signalling system failed at about 08:30, halting six trains, and that the Adif control centre ordered them at about 08:36 to resume normal running, calling the decision inexplicable [3][4]. Puente said one train had reminded the controller that protocol required running on sight at no more than 40 km/h, but the AVE was not told, and it covered 25 km before the impact [3]. Renfe suspended services between Madrid, Ciudad Real, and Andalusia [4].

Confidence is high on the collision, the toll, and the minister's account, reported on record by El País and the BBC; the cause rests on the government's preliminary account, and the speed at impact was not known by the cutoff.

items.title: Europe's Wholesale Gas Price Tops 100 Euros per Megawatt-Hour for First Time Since 2022
items.lede: Winter storage sits below last year's level while Gulf LNG cargoes stay scarce, and Dutch households on dynamic contracts feel the rise at once.

sections.text: Europe's benchmark wholesale gas price passed 100 euros per megawatt-hour on Wednesday, the highest level since the 2022 energy crisis that followed Russia's invasion of Ukraine, franceinfo and NOS reported [5][6]. The price was under 30 euros in February, before the United States and Israel began the war against Iran, NOS reported [6]. Franceinfo said the rise reflects lower storage than in 2025 ahead of winter, limited liquefied natural gas cargoes leaving the Gulf, and market fears of a new round of US strikes on Iran after the US midterm elections [5]. In the Netherlands, about 8 per cent of households on dynamic contracts pay the higher price at once [6]. No European Commission statement on the price was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the price level, reported by franceinfo and NOS; the market explanations are the outlets' own analysis.

items.title: Czech Students Call 3 November Strike Over Plan to Scrap Public-Media Fees
items.lede: Some 2,000 people rallied in Brno on Wednesday, and broadcast staff at Czech Television and Czech Radio have set a walkout for the same day.

sections.text: Thousands filled Prague's Old Town Square in the Czech Republic on Sunday to protest a coalition bill replacing Czech Television and Czech Radio licence fees with state funding, ČTK reported [7][8]. The lower house passed the bill in first reading on Saturday; it would cut their funding by about CZK 1.4 billion [7][8]. On Tuesday Prague's DAMU drama faculty declared an open-ended strike alert and will join the 3 November broadcaster strike [9]. On Tuesday evening the unions of the National Theatre's drama company declared a strike alert, demanding the withdrawal of the funding bill and the resignation of Culture Minister Oto Klempíř, who replied that the government supports culture [10]. Chamber speaker Tomio Okamura said he would back abolishing Czech Television and Czech Radio if someone proposed it, ČT24 reported [11]. On Monday afternoon Babiš also rejected Czech Radio director René Zavoral's call for a public debate, calling him an 'activist director' who should resign [12]. On Wednesday about 2,000 people protested in Brno, where a student committee called a nationwide strike for 3 November [13].
Confidence is high on the protests, the vote, and the strike calls, reported by ČTK, ČT24, and Expats.cz; the Brno figure is an official's estimate.

items.title: French Senate Passes Bill Making Rioters Pay for Protest Damage
items.lede: France also plans a compulsory 0.8 per cent insurance surcharge from January, pending Conseil d'État approval, as business groups put damage above one billion euros.

sections.text: France's Senate adopted the casseurs-payeurs bill early on Wednesday by 229 votes to 105, Public Sénat reported [14]. It makes everyone in a violent gathering jointly liable for damage, with the state able to claim up to 10,000 euros each, and allows seizure of welfare benefits from those who cannot pay [14]. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said on Saturday evening that the marches had gone smoothly despite a great many incidents of violence; on Sunday the ministry put arrests at 1,314, with 53 officers injured [15][16]. In Reims, the police watchdog IGPN was tasked with investigating after a police grenade seriously injured a marcher's shin on Saturday, franceinfo reported on Monday [17]. The Yellow Vests have called further protests for 31 Oct [16]. On Tuesday the Snes-FSU teachers' union said the government's Parcoursup concessions fall short and kept its call to march on 5 November [18]. On Wednesday franceinfo reported CCI France's estimate of over one billion euros in damage, and a planned compulsory 0.8 per cent riot surcharge on home, car, and business insurance from 1 January 2027, which the Conseil d'État must still validate [19].
Confidence is high on the vote, the surcharge, and the arrest figures, reported on record by Public Sénat and franceinfo; the damage estimate is CCI France's own.

items.title: Portugal's Ombudsman Demands Police Records on Baton Charges at Lisbon and Porto Housing Camps
items.lede: Prime Minister Luís Montenegro has now praised the officers' conduct as thousands of housing protesters massed outside parliament on Tuesday night.

sections.text: Portugal's Ombudsman, Luísa Neto, said on Monday she had urgently asked the PSP police's national directorate for documents on operations that began at about 02:00 on Sunday 25 October against housing-rights protesters camped in Lisbon's Praça D. Pedro IV and Porto's Praça D. João I, Lusa reported via RTP [20]. The interior ministry's inspectorate, IGAI, told Lusa it had opened an administrative inquiry into both operations, which left people injured [20]. The PSP dispersed the camps with batons and dogs after two hours of orders to leave, and reported 33 injured and 33 detained for disobedience; the organisers spoke of dozens injured [20]. On Tuesday evening Prime Minister Luís Montenegro praised the PSP's "careful" and "competent" work, RTP reported [21]. On Tuesday President António José Seguro called for dialogue on housing "and never violence" and said he awaited the inquiries into police conduct, Lusa reported via RTP [22]. Thousands rallied outside the Assembly of the Republic on Tuesday as the 2027 budget debate opened, and organisers said they would return to protest but not camp there [23].
Confidence is high on the ombudsman's request, the IGAI inquiry, the PSP figures, and the leaders' remarks, reported on record by Lusa and RTP; Tuesday's details rest on RTP summaries.

items.title: Italy's Salvini Vows to Press Cabinet to Halt Money and Weapons for Ukraine
items.lede: Defence Minister Guido Crosetto said Rome's line on Kyiv does not change, and Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said a new Italian aid package is ready.

sections.text: Italy's deputy prime minister Matteo Salvini was confirmed as secretary of the League on Sunday with 465 votes, 76% of the 611 valid ballots, against 146 for challenger Massimo Garavaglia, at the party's congress in Milan, La Stampa and ANSA reported [24][25][26]. Three ballots were blank and five invalid, and Salvini will lead the party until 2030 [25][24]. Before the vote, Salvini said that if confirmed he would tell the Council of Ministers to stop money and arms for Ukraine [27]. On Monday Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said a new military aid package for Kyiv was ready, ANSA reported [28]. Late on Monday ANSA reported that coalition allies had halted Salvini on Kyiv, with Defence Minister Guido Crosetto saying the line does not change and Meloni irritated by his congress remarks [29]. On Tuesday, in extracts from Bruno Vespa's book due out on 2 November, Salvini said challenger Massimo Garavaglia would join the League's secretariat if he agreed, ANSA reported [30].
Confidence is high on the vote and Salvini's statements, because La Stampa and ANSA report them on record; Crosetto's reply rests on an ANSA headline and summary.

items.title: Basque Police Arrest 17 After Student Riot in Bilbao
items.lede: Ten of those held are minors, all who saw a judge were freed on charges, and the groups behind the march have disowned the violence.

sections.text: Spain's Basque regional police, the Ertzaintza, have arrested 17 people over Monday night's riots in Bilbao, which followed a student demonstration against an event by the activist Vito Quiles that was finally not held, El País reported on Tuesday [31]. Ten of those detained are minors, one aged 14, and the rest are aged 18 to 25; a 22-year-old is also under investigation [31]. All who have appeared before a judge were released on charges, and none had a criminal record [31]. The police are working to identify more participants, while the groups that called the march have distanced themselves from the violence [31]. Basque government spokesperson María Ubarretxena said violence has no place in the Basque Country [31].
Confidence is high on the arrest figures, which El País attributes to the Ertzaintza; this rests on one outlet so far.

theaters.heading: Security, politics, and Russian pressure on Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania

items.title: Latvia's airBaltic Plans to Cut About 300 Pilots and Cabin Crew
items.lede: The union says every cabin crew post at the Riga base goes and staff learn their fate from Saturday, while the state airline says numbers may still change.

sections.text: Latvia's state airline airBaltic plans to make about 100 pilots and 200 cabin crew redundant, the Latvian Aviation Trade Union (LAA) announced and the airline confirmed, Latvian Television reported on Wednesday [1]. The union told LETA that pilots were informed on 27 October that about four in five would keep their jobs as the fleet shrinks to 36 aircraft [2]. All cabin crew posts at the Riga base will be cut, and staff will learn from Saturday whether their contracts are renewed [1] [2]. LAA board chair Dace Kavasa said the process is not in line with the law and called an offer of hiring preference for those who leave voluntarily an ultimatum [1]. Spokesperson Augusts Zilberts said the figures are not final, pilot cuts affect the Riga, Vilnius, and Tallinn bases, and Riga cabin crew may be offered posts in Vilnius and Tallinn [1]. The airline links the cuts to next year's flight volume; it earlier estimated 500 to 700 jobs could go [1].
Confidence is high on the planned figures, reported by LTV and LETA and confirmed on record by the airline's spokesperson; final numbers are pending the staff assessment.

items.title: Lithuania's Government Opposes Bill to Name Unconfessed KGB Collaborators
items.lede: The Defence Ministry, which drafted the opinion for parliament, calls the goal legitimate but says the Nemunas Dawn proposal would force disclosure of data officials do not collect.

sections.text: Lithuania's government on Wednesday rejected a bill by Nemunas Dawn leader Remigijus Žemaitaitis to publish the identities of former KGB collaborators who never confessed, LRT reported [3]. Parliament approved the bill at first reading in June 2025; the government's position goes to the Seimas [3]. The Defence Ministry said current law already provides for such publication [3]. The government also gave a negative opinion on a separate proposal to scrap the 75-year secrecy period for collaborators who confessed [3]. Žemaitaitis has claimed about 400 former KGB staff and collaborators work in the public sector without giving a source [3].
Confidence is moderate: the decision rests on one LRT report; the government's written opinion was not read.

items.title: Latvian Anti-Graft Bureau Detains Prime Minister Kulbergs' Adviser in EU Fraud Probe
items.lede: Mārtiņš Brencis, a newly elected United List MP, was dismissed the same day; an EPPO probe into €1.4 million in EU funds did not name him.

sections.text: Latvia's anti-corruption bureau KNAB detained Mārtiņš Brencis, Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs' adviser on public administration, on Wednesday in a criminal case run by the European Public Prosecutor's Office (EPPO), Latvian Television reported [4]. The prime minister's office confirmed the detention to the LETA news agency [5]. Kulbergs said he learned of it on Wednesday morning, assumed it related to Brencis' work before joining the government, and ordered his dismissal as adviser [4] [6]. Brencis, a former head of the Central Finance and Contracts Agency, was elected to the new Saeima for Kulbergs' United List and is due to take his seat next week [4]. The EPPO said KNAB searched in a probe of suspected procurement fraud in an Alūksne municipality project that may have obtained over €1.4 million from the European Regional Development Fund, without naming Brencis [4] [5]. Alūksne council chair Dzintars Adlers said no municipal employee was detained [6]. Latvian Radio reported that Brencis arrived at the Cabinet building shortly after 15:00 CET promising an explanation [5]; no statement from him was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the detention and dismissal, reported by LTV and LETA with the prime minister's office on record; the link between Brencis and the Alūksne case has not been confirmed by the EPPO.

items.title: Isamaa Lawyer Says No Verdict in Party Donation Case Before Estonia's March Election
items.lede: Prosecutors give the defence until next Monday to study the evidence before deciding on charges over €110,234 in allegedly prohibited donations, which the party denies.

sections.text: Estonia's opposition party Isamaa will face no court ruling in its criminal case before the March 2027 Riigikogu election, party lawyer Jaanus Tehver told ERR on Wednesday [7]. Prosecutors suspect Isamaa accepted €110,234 of about €330,000 in prohibited donations, mainly advertising services, between November 2020 and April 2024 [7]. Tehver said he expects charges and will file no further requests, and that at best a preliminary hearing could be held before the vote [7]. The Prosecutor's Office said the defence has until next Monday to examine the evidence, after which it will decide how to proceed [7]. Isamaa and the other suspects deny the allegations [7].
Confidence is moderate: one ERR report carries the lawyer's view and the prosecutors' statement; no court document was read.

items.title: Lithuania's First Post-Soviet Leader Vytautas Landsbergis Is Hospitalised
items.lede: His son confirmed the admission to Vilnius Santaros Clinics for tests, and LRT reports the 94-year-old was placed in intensive care.

sections.text: Vytautas Landsbergis, who led Lithuania after it broke from the Soviet Union, has been admitted to the Santaros Clinics in Vilnius for medical tests, LRT reported [8]. His son, Vytautas V. Landsbergis, confirmed the admission to LRT on Tuesday [8]. LRT reported that he had been placed in an intensive care unit [8]. Landsbergis turned 94 on 18 October [8]. No statement from the hospital was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the admission rests on one LRT report citing his son; the intensive care detail is LRT's own reporting and was not confirmed by the hospital.

items.title: Lithuania Seeks Consular Visit to Two Women Held in Iran Since 15 October
items.lede: Foreign Ministry chancellor Aistė Stakėnienė says no Lithuanian official has spoken to the detainees, and one woman's sister calls the alleged charges absurd.

sections.text: Lithuania's Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday that two Lithuanian women reported missing are being held in Iran, after Tehran informed it on 26 October [9] [10]. On Wednesday ministry chancellor Aistė Stakėnienė said Iran reported they were detained on 15 October and declined to give reasons [11]. LRT identified the women as Daiva Zakažauskaitė and Erika Šlimaitė, who were travelling together [11]. Stakėnienė said Lithuanian officials have not yet spoken with them and are seeking a consular visit to check their conditions, health, and access to a lawyer, likely through another EU member state's consular official [11]. Rūta Korsakienė, Zakažauskaitė's sister, said contact was lost after a desert excursion and described the alleged charges as absurd but potentially serious under Iranian law [11]. Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius said earlier that diplomatic work was under way to secure their release [9]. No Iranian statement on the charges was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the detention, confirmed by Lithuania's Foreign Ministry via BNS, ELTA, and LRT; the 15 October date and the charges rest on Lithuanian officials and relatives, with no Iranian source read.

items.title: Estonia's Security Police Chief Asks to Regain Bank Data Register Access
items.lede: KAPO head Margo Palloson argues the tracker rule does not bind security agencies on national-security work and vetting, and says no criminal-case queries were made since 1 October.
items.flag: FOLLOW UP TO PREVIOUS REPORT · single-source, unconfirmed

sections.text: Estonia's Justice Ministry cut the Police and Border Guard Board's and the Internal Security Service's (KAPO) access to the Enforcement Register, a state channel for querying bank data, after they missed a 1 October deadline to install a tracker that shows people who viewed their data [12] [13]. KAPO Director General Margo Palloson has now asked for access to the register and the e-arrest system to be restored, ERR News reported on Wednesday [13]. He argues the Code of Enforcement Procedure exempts security agencies from the tracker requirement for tasks under the Security Authorities Act and for security vetting [13]. He listed the data KAPO wants to query, including account existence, balances, statements, authorised users, beneficial owners, and safe deposit boxes [13]. Palloson said KAPO has made no register queries in criminal proceedings since 1 October [13]. The Tax and Customs Board and the Financial Intelligence Unit installed the tracker and regained access [13]. No Justice Ministry reply to the request was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: both developments rest on ERR reporting, which quotes the ministry's letter and Palloson's request; the letters themselves were not read.

items.title: Serbia Raises Terror Threat to Red After Knife Attack at Israeli Embassy
items.lede: A gendarme guarding the Belgrade mission shot dead the teenage attacker, whom security services had been monitoring as an Islamic State supporter.

sections.text: A minor attacked a Serbian Gendarmerie officer guarding Israel's embassy in Belgrade with two knives at 00:15 on Wednesday while shouting "Allahu Akbar", caretaker Interior Minister Ivica Dačić said [1] [2]. The officer suffered a minor cut to the face and shot the attacker dead in self-defence [1] [3]. Dačić said the attacker, not yet formally identified but believed to be from Šabac, was a Serbian citizen known to security services as an Islamic State supporter who had posted the group's flag on Instagram [1] [3]. Dačić raised the terrorism threat level to red, the highest, with tighter checks and more police at infrastructure sites and crowded places [1] [2]. Israel's Foreign Ministry said no embassy staff were hurt and the embassy was closed at the time [2]. The alert comes three days after snap elections in which the opposition Student List won a preliminary 52.85 per cent [2].
Confidence is high on the attack and the alert, which the Serbian government, BIRN, and the BBC all report; the attacker's identity and motive rest on the minister's account.

items.title: Bulgaria's Yotova and Gyurov Agree to One Live TV Debate Before the Run-Off
items.lede: Public broadcaster BNT hosts the only head-to-head on Thursday evening, after Gyurov accused the government of using official channels to campaign for the acting president.

sections.text: With all polling-station protocols processed, Bulgaria's Central Election Commission had acting President Iliana Yotova on 34.76 percent, former caretaker Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov on 31.95 percent and Revival leader Kostadin Kostadinov third, BNT reported [4]. Because no ticket won a majority, the commission on Tuesday formally set a 1 November run-off and said 1,525,034 of 6,584,025 eligible voters took part [5] [4]. On Monday Prime Minister Rumen Radev said voters would choose between peace and war, casting Gyurov's pro-EU, pro-Ukraine stance as warmongering [6]. The government's Facebook page and press office carried the line "Let's vote for Iliana Iotova so Bulgaria can be in safe hands," and Gyurov said this breached the electoral code; the election commission has been notified [7]. Public broadcaster BNT said on Wednesday that the two will meet in the campaign's only televised debate on 29 October at 21:00 Sofia time (20:00 CET), moderated by Poli Zlatareva [8] [9]. In a draw on Wednesday the election commission gave Gyurov the first slot for 10-minute addresses on 30 October, the last day of campaigning [8].
Confidence is high on the results, run-off date, and debate, reported by BNT, BTA, The Sofia Globe, and Novinite; the dispute over official channels rests on one BIRN report.

items.title: Albania's Student Protests Thin on Their 16th Day as Rama Refuses to Quit
items.lede: Fewer students and lecturers turned out on Wednesday, after more than 270 arrests, while the prime minister's offer of talks still found no takers.

sections.text: Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama on Sunday announced a package against "violence and urban anarchy" after weeks of clashes in Tirana, blaming opposition leader Sali Berisha, "Antifa extremists", and foreign actors [10]. It would fine participants in unauthorized gatherings €100 to €1,000, and make organizing a banned gathering a criminal offense [10]. Public broadcaster RTSH reported on Monday that in 13 days of protests police had arrested more than 270 people, prosecuted 344, and suspended nine officers for excessive force [11]. The Health Ministry said on 19 October that 310 people had been injured since the protests began, including 191 police officers, Albanian Daily News reported [12]. On Tuesday, the 15th day, protesters marched to the Prime Minister's Office without significant incidents, RTSH reported [13]. On Wednesday, the 16th day, CNA reported a low turnout of students and lecturers outside the Education Ministry, with police and water cannon trucks deployed and no clashes by late morning; Rama, whose invitations to dialogue students have repeatedly rejected, again ruled out resigning [14].
Confidence is moderate: the law's terms are Rama's announcement relayed by BIRN, arrest figures are official, and Wednesday's turnout rests on CNA alone.

items.title: Armenia's Parliament Ratifies US Framework Deal on the Trump Route
items.lede: Only the ruling Civil Contract backed the pact, which gives a US-led company 74 per cent of the corridor's operator while Yerevan keeps border and customs control.

sections.text: Armenia's parliament on Wednesday ratified a framework agreement with the United States on the Trump Route (TRIPP), meant to link mainland Azerbaijan with its Nakhchivan exclave, with only the ruling Civil Contract voting in favour and the opposition against, OC Media reported [1]. Under the deal the US would hold 74 per cent of the TRIPP Development Company and Armenia 26 per cent, while Armenia keeps legislative, judicial, security, border, tax, and customs authority [1]. Contracted private operators would staff a "front office" handling documents and fees, with decisions left to Armenian officials [1]. Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan said the route could open before a peace treaty with Azerbaijan is signed; the opposition Armenia Alliance said the text reflects Azerbaijan's interests more than Armenia's [1]. No Azerbaijani reaction was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the vote and terms come from one OC Media report; News.am carried a matching headline but its text was not read.

items.title: Azerbaijan Hands Former Aliyev Aide Ramiz Mehdiyev a Suspended 14-Year Term
items.lede: The 88-year-old former head of Aliyev's administration avoids prison on age and health grounds but loses his assets after a treason and coup-plot conviction.

sections.text: An Azerbaijani court sentenced Ramiz Mehdiyev, who ran the presidential administration from 1995 to 2019, to 14 years in prison, suspended because of his age and health, OC Media reported on Wednesday [2]. The charges included treason, attempting to seize power by force, money laundering, and bribery [2]. The court ordered his assets confiscated without disclosing which, and provided for a move to strip his state awards [2]. The State Security Service had accused him of plotting with foreign intelligence services to overthrow the government, including passing a governance-reform paper to opposition leader Ali Karimli, and of laundering more than 17 million manat [2]. Analysts have questioned the published evidence and see the case as part of President Ilham Aliyev's consolidation of power [2]. No court or prosecutor statement was read by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the verdict rests on one OC Media report; no Azerbaijani official text was read.

items.title: Georgian Appeals Judge Approves Plea Deals Freeing Four 4 October Protest Organizers
items.lede: Opposition politician Murtaz Zodelava and reserve colonel Lasha Beridze will leave prison in November, while Paata Burchuladze and two others without deals stay behind bars.

sections.text: Tamar Lomtatidze, a judge at Georgia's Tbilisi Court of Appeals, on Wednesday approved plea agreements for four people jailed over the 4 October 2025 anti-government clashes in Tbilisi, OC Media reported [3]. They are Murtaz Zodelava and Lasha Beridze, named as members of the protest's "organising committee", and protesters Guri Zhvania and Irakli Chkhvirkia [3]. Each pleaded guilty and received three years and one month, of which one year and one month is custodial, so all four are due out during November [3]. More than 60 people have been convicted in the case; committee members Burchuladze, Paata Manjgaladze, and Irakli Nadiradze have no deals and remain jailed [3].
Confidence is moderate: the ruling comes from one OC Media report citing the agency IPN; no court statement was read.

items.title: Georgia's Coalition for Change Tells Judges the Party-Ban Suit Lacks Evidence
items.lede: Coalition for Change argued that refusing to recognise election results is no ground for a ban, with hearings scheduled to run to 30 October.

sections.text: Georgia's Constitutional Court began substantive hearings on Monday on a lawsuit by 88 Georgian Dream MPs to declare five opposition parties unconstitutional: Unity – National Movement, Coalition for Change, Lelo – Strong Georgia, Gakharia for Georgia, and the Federalists [4]. The suit accuses them of seeking to overthrow the constitutional order; all five deny it [4]. The court partly granted a final defense motion on evidence but refused to call Bidzina Ivanishvili, Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze, and other ruling-party figures as witnesses [4]; The Messenger confirmed the partial evidence ruling and the refusal to summon Ivanishvili [5]. On Tuesday, day five, three National Movement representatives closed its defense; Ana Tsitlidze called the suit "political gossip, myths and manipulation" and questioned the judges' impartiality [6]. On Wednesday Coalition for Change presented its defense; member Tengiz Tevzadze said the suit cites no party statements or concrete violence tied to the party or its members, and Maia Kopaleishvili called the parliamentary inquiry commission's findings an assertion by the claimants rather than evidence [7]. Coalition representative Giga Lemonjava argued that refusing to recognize election results is not grounds for a ban [8].
Confidence is high on the court's earlier rulings, reported by JAMnews and The Messenger; Wednesday's arguments rest on AdjaraTV and Publika alone.

items.title: Netherlands Offers Help to Armenian Exporters Squeezed by Russian Curbs
items.lede: Visiting Dutch Foreign Minister Berendsen also pledged money to trace people missing from the conflict with Azerbaijan, but sidestepped questions on Armenians held in Baku.

sections.text: Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen said in Yerevan on Tuesday that the Netherlands wants to help Armenian businesses, including flower growers, find markets outside Russia, citing difficulties caused by Russian economic restrictions, JAMnews reported [9]. Speaking alongside Armenian Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan, he urged Armenia to use the EU's autonomous trade measures, approved on 24 September, which remove duties on about 80% of its exports to the EU for two years [9]. He said the Armenia–Azerbaijan peace process must end in a signed agreement and offered Dutch funding for work on the fate of people missing on both sides, which Mirzoyan welcomed [9]. Asked about Armenian prisoners in Baku, Berendsen did not answer directly [9]. No Azerbaijani reaction was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the remarks come from one JAMnews account of the news conference; no Dutch or Armenian ministry readout was read.

items.title: Germany Plans First Rise in Parental Allowance Since 2007
items.lede: Family Minister Karin Prien's new draft drops a planned cut to 12 months, and the four months reserved for each parent would pay 80 instead of 65 percent of income.

sections.text: Germany's family ministry plans to raise the minimum parental allowance from 300 to 330 euros a month and the maximum from 1,800 to 1,900 euros, the first increase since it began in 2007 [1] [2]. A draft bill has gone into consultation within the government, so nothing is decided yet [1]. An earlier draft cut the maximum period from 14 to 12 months; it now stays at 14 when both parents take at least four months each [1] [2] [3]. The four reserved months would pay 80 percent of prior net income instead of 65 percent, and the remaining months only 50 percent [2]. Family Minister Karin Prien (CDU) told ARD it was not a U-turn and that savings would be smaller than under the original plan [3].
Confidence is high on the planned rates and duration, reported by dpa via the Stuttgarter Zeitung, Deutschlandfunk, and tagesschau from the ministry.

items.title: German Cabinet Widens Insider Sabotage Screening at Critical Infrastructure
items.lede: Rail, grid-restart, water, and LNG staff face reliability checks with domestic intelligence involvement, as Berlin points to Russia's sabotage threat since 2022.

sections.text: Germany's federal cabinet on Wednesday adopted a revised ordinance that widens security screening of employees in critical infrastructure, aiming to cut the risk of sabotage by extremists or on behalf of foreign intelligence services [4] [5]. Newly covered are operators of plants that can restart the power grid after a total blackout, digital energy systems above three gigawatts, large waterworks, and LNG terminals [4] [5]. Screening checks reliability, such as signs of extremism or vulnerability to blackmail, requires the employee's consent, and involves the domestic intelligence agency BfV [4]. The government cited the rising threat of attacks below the threshold of war, above all from Russia since 2022; the Bundestag had already tightened the screening law in December [4].
Confidence is high on the decision and its scope, reported by tagesschau and dpa via the Süddeutsche Zeitung.

items.title: Mercedes-Benz Car Profit More Than Halves as China Sales Slump
items.lede: The Stuttgart carmaker had already cut its 2026 outlook on Tuesday, now expecting a 2 to 3 percent car margin, and will review its China strategy.

sections.text: Stuttgart-based Mercedes-Benz, one of Germany's largest carmakers, said on Wednesday that its car division's adjusted return on sales fell to 2.5 percent in July to September from 4.8 percent a year earlier [6] [7]. The division's operating profit fell to 560 million euros, less than half the prior-year figure, and deliveries in China dropped 31 percent to 86,800 vehicles [6]. Group net profit rose almost 28 percent to 1.52 billion euros because the prior year carried job-cut charges, while adjusted operating profit fell 15 percent and revenue fell 4.5 percent to 30.7 billion euros [7] [8]. Chief executive Ola Källenius said conditions had become even more challenging, especially in China [6]. On Tuesday Mercedes had already cut its 2026 outlook, now expecting an adjusted car return on sales of 2 to 3 percent, and it will review its China strategy [6].
Confidence is high on the figures, which tagesschau, the Stuttgarter Zeitung, and Deutschlandfunk report from the company's results.

items.title: Baden-Württemberg Police Brace for Saturday's Gen Z Youth Protests
items.lede: Stuttgart city saw no legal basis for a ban, while the state criminal police office is in contact with French authorities after riots in France.

sections.text: Youth demonstrations called by the 'Gen Z regelt' initiative are planned on Saturday in Stuttgart, Karlsruhe, Freiburg, Ulm, Mannheim, and other cities in Germany's Baden-Württemberg, the Stuttgarter Zeitung reported with dpa [9]. Stuttgart has 500 participants officially registered, though well over 10,000 signalled online that they would attend; the initiative rejects violence [9]. Police in Stuttgart cited signs of possible disruption, Ulm police warned that Halloween revellers could join the crowds, and the state criminal police office is involved and in contact with French authorities [9]. Interior Minister Manuel Hagel (CDU) said peaceful protest would be protected and violence met firmly [9]. Stuttgart city said there was no legal basis for a ban, as there were no concrete signs of riots like those in France [9].
Confidence is high on the plans and official statements as reported, but they rest on a single dpa-based report in the Stuttgarter Zeitung.

items.title: IG Metall Rejects Employers' First Offer for Germany's 3.7 Million Metalworkers
items.lede: Warning strikes can begin on Sunday when the peace obligation ends, after talks also failed in Bavaria, Lower Saxony, Baden-Württemberg, and, on Wednesday, the Hesse-Rhineland-Palatinate-Saarland region.

sections.text: Germany's IG Metall union on Tuesday rejected the first offer from metal and electrical industry employers in regional talks covering just over 3.7 million workers [10] [11]. Employers in five bargaining regions jointly offered, for the first time, a one-off payment of 1 percent of annual pay in July 2027 and a permanent 1.3 percent rise in July 2028, with a contract running to the end of 2028 [10] [11]. North Rhine-Westphalia district head Knut Giesler called it a de facto minus round; the Lower Saxony district said warning strikes from 1 November were unavoidable [10]. Gesamtmetall president Udo Dinglreiter said job losses and deindustrialisation had to be stopped [10]. Südwestmetall said almost half of Baden-Württemberg firms, 45 percent, would not have to pay the one-off sum under a hardship clause [11]. On Wednesday, talks for the Mitte region covering Hesse, Rhineland-Palatinate, and Saarland, with about 388,000 workers, also failed in Hanau; district head Jörg Köhlinger called the repeated offer "lousy" and said warning strikes there would start from 00:01 on Sunday, 1 November, while employers' negotiator Ralph Wangemann called it "constructive and appropriate" [12] [13].
Confidence is high on the offer terms, the rejection, and the strike timetable, reported by tagesschau and dpa via the FAZ from union and employer statements.

items.title: Hesse's CDU Leader Ines Claus Emerges as a Contender for Germany's Presidency
items.lede: Merz's circle told ARD he sees the right to nominate with his CDU rather than the CSU, which proposed Ilse Aigner, but he has not yet decided.

sections.text: Ines Claus, 49, who leads the CDU group in Hesse's state parliament and is a deputy federal CDU chair, told the Rheinische Post on Tuesday it was a great honour to be named as a possible successor to President Frank-Walter Steinmeier [14]. The paper cited senior CDU sources calling her Chancellor Friedrich Merz's favourite, which his circle clearly denied, saying he had neither decided nor made a proposal [14]. The CSU has so far proposed Bavarian parliament speaker Ilse Aigner; CDU bodies are due to discuss the question on 9 November, and the Federal Convention votes on 30 January [15]. On Wednesday, Chancellor Friedrich Merz's circle told ARD he sees the right to nominate with the CDU, the largest party in the Federal Convention, but has not decided [16] [17]. He plans talks with CDU state premiers and the CSU first, then with the SPD and the Greens [16].

Confidence is high on Claus's statement, the Merz camp denial, and his nomination stance, reported by dpa via the Tagesspiegel and by tagesschau. Confidence is moderate on her standing in the party, which rests on unnamed sources.

items.title: German Environment Minister Says Audi's U.S. Plant Bets on a Dead Horse
items.lede: Criticism of Döllner's Georgia rally appearance now reaches the federal cabinet, days before Audi reports third-quarter figures on Friday.

sections.text: German carmaker Audi, part of Volkswagen, plans a $4.2 billion, 4,500-job first U.S. plant in Georgia, which President Trump announced at a Republican rally on Saturday with Audi chief Gernot Döllner onstage [18] [19] [20]. VW works council head Daniela Cavallo and IG Metall chief Christiane Benner accused Döllner of breaching Audi's neutrality rules [21] [22]. Baden-Württemberg's premier Cem Özdemir said anyone investing in Georgia must say what happens in Neckarsulm [20], where A5 and A6 output is due to end in late 2033 [23]. In an internal letter seen by dpa, Döllner wrote on Tuesday that Audi was asked to present the plans with the president, decided solely in the company's interest, and that its U.S. business is not profitable today [24]. In a YouGov poll of 2,725 adults on 26 October, 57 percent called the appearance inappropriate and 18 percent appropriate [24]. A German government spokesperson declined to comment, calling it a business decision [22]. Federal Environment Minister Carsten Schneider (SPD) told the Kölner Stadt-Anzeiger that Audi was betting on fossil fuels, a dead horse [25] [26]. Audi reports third-quarter figures on Friday [25].

Confidence is high on the quotes and the plant plan, reported by tagesschau, The Guardian, stern, and the Kölner Stadt-Anzeiger. Confidence is moderate on any rule breach, which rests on labor leaders' reading.

items.title: Germany Narrows Its Nuclear Waste Repository Search to Under 5% of Its Territory
items.lede: Six states have now dropped out entirely, Baden-Württemberg's Ulm region is also out, and the Bundestag will have the final say on the site.

sections.text: Germany's federal repository company BGE said on Tuesday that areas it considers geologically suitable for a high-level nuclear waste repository now cover less than five percent of the country, and that all of Germany has now been assessed [27]. Rhineland-Palatinate, Hesse, Berlin, Saxony, Hamburg, and Saarland are no longer part of the search; Saxony, Berlin, Hamburg, and Hesse were dropped this year [27]. In 2020 the company had named 90 sub-areas covering almost 54 percent of Germany; granite, salt, and clay are considered potentially suitable host rocks [27]. In Baden-Württemberg, the Ulm region was rated well suited but not among the best areas and has dropped out, the Stuttgarter Zeitung reported [28]. The BGE plans to propose five to ten regions for surface exploration by the end of 2027; the ratings are not legally binding, and the Bundestag decides the final site [28] [27].

Confidence is high on the narrowing and the states dropped, which tagesschau reports from a BGE press release. Confidence is high on the Ulm rating, reported by the Stuttgarter Zeitung from the same BGE announcement.
